source.title: Anuhea - Higher Than The Clouds (Official Video)

review: M. Delacroix (a Parisian salon critic, 1842): I am pleased that the phrases close properly, with honest cadences; the voices move with propriety; the melody sits squarely on the beat. I struggled to follow a clear tune.

slider.label: a classical piece with tidbits of the song

layers.text: Only the skeleton of the tune is kept (its strong-beat notes). The notes in between are re-composed as classical scale passages.
The bass is re-written as a period bass line (walking, Alberti or sustained).
The original backing is replaced by the composer's own accompaniment textures over (re-)harmonised chords.
No drums. Timpani only mark the big cadences, as in a real score.

song.title: Anuhea - Higher Than The Clouds (Official Video)

era.name: Romantic
era.summary: Emotion first: long singing melodies, rich and colourful harmony, flexible tempo (rubato), big dynamic swells and larger orchestras.
traits: Rubato: tempo breathes, slowing at phrase ends
Wide piano arpeggios held by the sustain pedal
Richer chords: borrowed chords, diminished sevenths, chromatic colour
Huge dynamic range, from whisper to full orchestra
era.instruments: Grand piano, full string sections, clarinets, horns, harp, expanded brass and percussion
why: All three eras were tried. Romantic scored best (Romantic 1.099, Baroque 1.096, Classical 1.049). The score combines how classical it sounds, how much of the song survives, and how well the song suits the composer.
Some chords fall outside the plain key, which Romantic harmony welcomes.

composer.name: Felix Mendelssohn
composer.bio: Light, quicksilver Romanticism: sparkling fast strings, clear forms, elegant lyricism.
reasons: its overall character scored highest for this style
applied: Pulsing string chords, horns and harp swell under the melody in the loud sections
An independent counter-melody weaves around the tune (counterpoint 62%)
Re-harmonised more freely toward the composer's harmonic language

top.name: Bach
reasons: its fairly even energy suits a steady, unbroken style

top.name: Beethoven
reasons: it is in a minor key, which Beethoven favoured for dramatic or tender music

ensemble.name: Orchestra
ensemble.summary: String sections plus woodwinds, horns or trumpets, timpani (and harp in Romantic style).
why: In this composer's style it scored best of the four ensembles: Orchestra 1.099, String quartet 1.055, Solo keyboard 1.051, Chamber ensemble 0.989.
Why it works: the full colour palette: the song's loud choruses can swell into the whole orchestra.
The violins i carries the vocal melody (E4–Eb5). It was moved by octaves into the instrument's most singing register, with the key unchanged.

changes.dropped: The drum kit, synths and electric bass are gone. Their rhythmic drive now comes from the accompaniment patterns.
